title: Your Side of the Duvet
subject: a man in Leeds whose wife rolls the whole duvet around herself every night; he buys a second duvet just for himself, and every morning she is under his one anyway
caption: Raspy blue-eyed soul pop, mid-2020s radio ballad style. Rhodes electric piano holding slow gospel-tinged chords, an upright piano doubling the hook, fingerstyle electric bass, a brushed drum kit with a soft backbeat, Hammond organ swells under the choruses. Warm live-room mix with light tape saturation and a close vocal. Male baritone with a gritty raspy belt, hushed verses rising to full-chest choruses. 74 BPM, E-flat major. Tender, warm and quietly amused. No trap drums, no autotune, no EDM drop, no gospel choir takeover, no country twang.
lyrics:
[Intro - Rhodes and brushed kit]

[Verse 1]
Three a.m., the window's open wide
You roll over and pull it to your side
Wrapped up like a sausage roll in white
I'm on the edge in my socks all night

[Pre-Chorus]
I could wake you, I could pull it back
But your face is doing that

[Chorus]
Take your side of the duvet
Take my side too
I'll freeze till Monday, darling
If it's keeping you

[Verse 2]
So I bought my own, a single, navy blue
Twenty quid from Dunelm, brand new
Folded neat beside you on the bed
Morning comes, it's round your head

[Chorus]
Take your side of the duvet
Take the navy too
I'll buy a third one, darling
And you'll take that too

[Bridge - organ swell]
Cold feet on my knees
That's the deal, I guess

[Chorus]
Take your side of the duvet
Take my side too
I'll freeze for twenty winters
If I'm next to you

[Outro - Rhodes alone]
Three a.m., the window's open wide
Keep it, love, I'm fine
